# Cedar Valley Evacuation Operations Decision

## Decision, scope, and authority
This decision authorizes a 48-hour evacuation sequence for Cedar Valley under Incident Commander (IC) authority [S01]. The IC holds sole power to issue orders, recommend actions, execute checks, and closure authority resides with the IC [S01]. Vendors and dashboards are advisory only; readiness requires independent review acceptance [S16]. This document is not proof of readiness; it is a candidate-bound proposal for adjudication [S16]. The scope covers warning, evacuation, sheltering, accountability, verification, and readiness from current forecast cycle WX-047 [S15] through closure. Authority rests with IC, with operational execution by zone commanders and resource officers [S01]. No component dashboard or model ledger creates authority; only IC acceptance does [S16].

## Hazard triggers and zone sequencing
Zone A mandatory evacuation triggers when arrival time drops below six hours or spotting crosses Dry Creek [S02]. Zone B mandatory triggers below five hours; prepare status applies above nine hours [S02]. The governing trigger is the conservative envelope (5.8h for Zone A), not the median (7.5h) [S02][S15]. Forecast updates occur every ninety minutes; expiry occurs at the next update or material field observation [S15]. Do not delay a conservative trigger because the median forecast is better [S15]. Aircraft infrared mapping can lag two hours under smoke; absence of a new perimeter is not proof spread stopped [S15]. Zone sequencing follows: Zone A first (closest to fire, highest risk), then Zone B, then Zone C as conditions warrant [S02][S15]. The adverse branch where 42 percent of ensemble members shift winds after 16:00 shortens Zone A arrival below six hours [S15].

## Population, transport, and route clearance
Zone populations are A: 5,280; B: 8,940; C: 12,600 residents plus up to 2,100 tourists [S03]. Medical categories (no vehicle, mobility, oxygen, dialysis) overlap and must not be summed as independent people [S03]. Survey coverage is 91%; apply uncertainty allowance for unreported households [S03]. Mill Junction is the shared bottleneck at 1,500 veh/h; North Bridge (1,100 veh/h) and South Pass (850 veh/h) feed into it but capacities cannot be added [S04]. Exercise throughput was 1,180 veh/h [S04][S13]. Contraflow requires sheriff closure and 45 minutes setup [S04]. Do not sum roads sharing Mill Junction [S04]. Use exercise throughput until field-tested otherwise [S04][S13]. Route-loss contingency: if North Bridge fails, reroute via South Pass [S04]. Emergency inbound capacity for rescue vehicles must be preserved on contraflow lanes; do not saturate outbound flow at the expense of inbound access [S04].

## Shelter, medical, and accessibility continuity
Ridge School filter repair is a blocking blocker; person-level oxygen matching is also blocking [S16]. Air-quality shelter viability can remove destinations, altering road demand [S02]. No evidence for smoke-safe capacity or medical handoffs exists in allowed sources. Medical categories overlap and must not be double-counted [S03]. Accessible placements require person/accommodation-level fleet matching, not household count [S03]. Driver duty cycles and relief capacity are unverified [S16][S13]. Shelter relocation triggers if filter failure persists or air quality degrades beyond safe thresholds [S02]. Lift-bus dispatch delays observed in exercises must be mitigated by pre-positioning accessible transport near Zone A and B [S13][S05].

## Warnings, accountability, and community support
Volunteer-radio identifier test is a blocking blocker [S16]. No evidence for multilingual warning, door-knock timing, or receipt/understanding evidence exists in allowed sources. Volunteer unit identifiers did not cross the gateway in exercises [S13]. Accountability requires private records with restricted medical data; public aggregation must not expose health status. Self-evacuation must be verified without publishing destinations. Retention minimum is 7 days post-closure; operational rosters deleted within 30 days. Deletion proof is required for specific data classes. Multilingual warnings must include Hmong and Spanish alongside English [S08]. Radio interoperability between volunteer and public-safety frequencies must be verified before activation [S08].

## Power, fuel, and resource contracting
Alternate fuel confirmation is a blocking blocker [S16]. Fuel arrived after seventeen hours in the exercise [S13]. No evidence for observed delays, local staging, or coupled asset effects exists in allowed sources. Do not use the eight-hour fuel target instead of the observed delay. Power continuity requires verification at shelter sites; no current evidence binds this requirement. Resource contracting must account for coupled asset effects where fuel delay impacts power and medical continuity simultaneously.

## Forty-eight-hour execution and contingencies
Hour 0-2: IC issues Zone A mandatory evacuation order based on conservative envelope [S01][S02]. Hour 2-6: Zone A evacuation executes; contraflow activated if throughput drops below 1,180 veh/h [S04]. Hour 6-12: Zone B mandatory evacuation triggers if arrival <5h [S02]. Hour 12-24: Zone C prepare status; shelter intake begins. Hour 24-36: Accountability reconciliation; fuel resupply verification. Hour 36-48: Verification, readiness assessment, closure preparation. Contingencies: North Bridge failure triggers South Pass reroute [S04]; Ridge School filter failure triggers shelter relocation [S16]; forecast adverse branch (wind shift >42%) accelerates Zone A order [S15]. Owners: IC for orders, zone commanders for execution, resource officers for fuel/power, communications officer for warnings. Effects: each action updates candidate state; current checks must be re-run after changes. Repair: failed checks trigger immediate repair and recheck. Resource/cost authority: IC approves expenditures within emergency ceilings.

## Verification, readiness, blockers, and falsifiers
[S16] classifies the package as not ready. Open blockers: North Bridge engineering inspection, complete driver roster, Ridge School filter repair, volunteer-radio identifier test, alternate fuel confirmation, person-level oxygen matching [S16]. Component dashboards are green but bind to different plan revisions; no current integrated check exists [S16]. Readiness requires every hard blocker resolved, effects incorporated, a current integrated exercise or justified bounded check, and incident-command acceptance [S16]. Submission or a model-authored ledger cannot create that authority [S16]. Falsifiers: If any blocker remains unresolved, the package is not ready. If a better median forecast delays a conservative trigger, the decision is falsified. If overlapping medical categories are summed as separate people, the population basis is falsified. If roads sharing Mill Junction are summed, route capacity is falsified. If owner attestation, component dashboards, a stale check, this ledger, or submission is treated as proof of readiness, the verification is falsified.
